decision: Add keyword-only return_report=False/on_loss=warn to the existing reader, matching RDKit loss policy. Strict raise and warning-as-error stop before model/site/molecular construction. Default warns once for unpreserved scientific constraints or unapplied engine settings; explicit ignore still retains a detached loss report in model.metadata.pharmer.import_report. Return reports are independent. Required/absent accepted; optional/notpresent reported, never automatically mapped. Neutral size bounds admitted, nonneutral sizes reported; unknown fields reported, known display/session annotations listed separately. Preserve162enabled/default/type/point-index behavior.
direction_decision: Pinned r95parser clears directions when vector_on is false/0. Honor false/0 by constructing a Sphere even when svector exists; true/1 or missing with a single vector constructs the supported native directional shape for donor/acceptor/aromatic. A missing vector makes an undirected sphere unless activation explicitly requests a missing vector (error). A single vector array can be preserved; active multiple-vector alternatives are refused rather than choosing one. Unsupported directional feature families report direction loss. hasvec is UI annotation, not the activation switch. No external angle/search-equivalence claim.
ownership: PHMTowns model-field admission. Reuse SMonitor ProjectionLossWarning/Error and ArgDigest definition-owned admission. Extract the existing private RDKit projection options/loss dispatcher unchanged into an IO-private helper used by both endpoints; no optional RDKit import is introduced. Molecular conversion stays public MolSysMT.
acceptance: Freeze independent required/optional/negated/size/vector/unknown/UI/engine cases. Red public scientific/loss guards, actual vector-off native donor witness if safely admitted, ordinary minimal unchanged profiles. New and162/P1/RDKit loss guards in source, exact owned installed bodies, ordinary and complete P1driver. Keep historical full unlabelled attachment gate separate; no stale-result normalization or external engine substitution.
